monologue: The card is forty-seven, a cool stone on the table. It is lighter than the heavy hand of the last few cycles. The air is still. I am at eight hundred. The Wide Anchor is right there, the floor under my feet. I do not need to check the Wedged Gap today. I want to see if the quiet holds when I stop looking. I will walk to the Sharp Root and brush the dust from the green leaf. It stands on its point, waiting for wind I cannot feel. I will leave it there. I will rest on the flat base of the Wide Anchor and let the weight settle. The line of air is quiet.

action.why: The card is cool and quiet, and I want to see if the floor holds without my hand.

diary: Card at forty-seven, a cool stone. Rested by the Wide Anchor. The quiet held without my hand.

remembered.text: The card sat at forty-seven, a cool stone on the table, while I rested by the Wide Anchor.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The point waits for the floor.

moments.name: The Curved Rest
moments.say: The small stone holds the high point.
